headline: Tuesday: college basketball's opening night, midweek MACtion (Akron @ Ohio, Miami (OH) vs Buffalo), Champions League (Atlético vs Bayern at noon PT), and NHL. No NBA today (Election Day).

sections.label: Best of the Day
sections.slate: The strongest edges across today's card. Monday these went 0-1. Today two sources agree on Ohio and on Buffalo.

straight.reasoning: RG.org and Action Network both lay the points. Ohio leads the MAC in rushing (192 yards a game), and Akron allows 186 a game and ranks 119th in rushing success rate allowed. Akron is 1-7 with six straight losses, and six of its seven FBS losses were by 15 or more. QB Nick Poulos is playing well since returning. Risk: Ohio has played down to weak teams before (13-10 at Kent State). Playable at -13.5; skip at -14.

RG.org takes Buffalo +6.5, and Action Network likes Buffalo's team total Over, so both expect Buffalo to move the ball. Buffalo has scored 23+ in three straight behind its run game, Miami's pass defense allows 270 yards a game, and Miami has won three of its four FBS games by 3 or fewer. Kickoff times differ between sources, so check your book. Skip at +5.5.

parlay.title: MACtion Double
parlay.reasoning: The two MAC plays where sources agree. Pays about 2.6-to-1.

sections.label: NBA
sections.slate: No NBA games today. The league doesn't schedule games on Election Day to encourage voting. The NBA is back tomorrow and will be the main sport on the board from here on. College basketball picks are on the College Hoops tab.

sections.label: College Hoops
sections.slate: College basketball opening week. Lines on brand-new rosters are the least reliable of the year, and no two sources agreed on a game today, so every pick is a quarter unit at confidence 1.

straight.reasoning: Wofford is ranked 240+ spots lower, and Tennessee's new offensive talent, led by Juke Harris, should pile up points. The writer says the line is too low and still shrinking. Action Network's pick.

Stetson already has a game under its belt (it played Clemson last night and scored well inside), while South Carolina has 12 new players and is expected to play slow, which keeps the score closer. VSiN's pick.
Dimers' model gives Manhattan a 56% chance to cover. In opening-week blowouts, the favorite often empties its bench late, which helps big underdogs cover.
This is Dimers' biggest edge of the day across all sports: 60% model cover probability. Same logic as Manhattan: a huge number in an opener.

sections.label: Football
sections.slate: Tuesday MACtion: Akron @ Ohio (4:00 PM PT) and Buffalo @ Miami (OH). Thursday Night Football is next for the NFL.

straight.reasoning: MAC's best rushing offense against a bad run defense, and Akron has lost six straight by mostly big margins. Two sources agree. Skip at -14.
Buffalo's offense is rolling, and Miami's wins have been close. Two sources lean Buffalo. Skip at +5.5.

sections.label: Hockey
sections.slate: Tuesday card includes Stars @ Capitals (4:00 PM PT).

straight.reasoning: Dallas allows a league-low 2.14 goals a game with a 93.6% penalty kill, and Stars games average 4.93 goals. Washington's games run higher (6.62), which is the risk. RG.org's pick. Quarter unit at plus money.

sections.label: Soccer
sections.slate: Champions League: Atlético Madrid vs Bayern Munich at 12:00 PM PT.

straight.event: Champions League · Atlético Madrid vs Bayern
straight.reasoning: Both defenses are strong, and Bayern has drawn two of three Champions League games and three of eight league matches. +290 implies about 25.6%, which RG.org thinks is too low. Quarter unit. Skip below +260.
